Find the darkest country on this map. Then look for the next-darkest tier. The gap between them is the whole story of global military spending.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The map shows total military spending in 2025, in inflation-adjusted US dollars. Data: Our World in Data (CC BY). The top band starts above $500 billion, and only one country sits in it.
2/ That country is the United States. China and Russia sit in the next band down, which runs from $100 billion to $500 billion, alongside several other big spenders.
3/ SIPRI put total world military expenditure at about $2.7 trillion in 2024, up 9.4% on the previous year.
4/ Absolute dollars hide the burden. As a share of GDP in 2024, Israel spent about 8.8% and Russia about 7.1%, against roughly 3.4% for the US and 1.7% for China.
5/ Look at Africa on the map: most countries sit in the palest bands, under $2 billion. Algeria is the clear exception, a dark patch on the northwest of the continent.
6/ Europe has been getting darker. Germany stands out on the map as one of the heaviest spenders on the continent, a sharp change from its post-Cold War posture.
7/ Is the world spending too much, too little, or on the wrong things? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
